matches.gold_text: Proposals must be received by the City by 3:00 p.m. PT on September 17, 2024.
Proposals must not be submitted by fax.
The vendor must offer ERP software and services that satisfy all of the City's functional and technical requirements.
The preferred vendor has experience successfully implementing the proposed solutions for cities of similar size and scope of services.
Any best-of-breed Human Capital Management solution offered must be able to integrate with the selected ERP system.
A vendor responding with a best-of-breed solution must complete the Section 6 Requirements template for the relevant functionality and submit it per the Section 5 instructions.
The vendor must provide an integrated ERP solution that includes the modules and functionality defined in the Requirements document.
The replacement ERP solution is to be implemented in phases or as recommended by the selected vendor and approved by the City.
Vendors invited to demonstrate their product should be prepared to discuss the application's best practices and its ability to adapt to user preferences.
The City's estimated implementation window runs from March 2025 through January 2027.
All modules in scope must go live by January 1, 2027.
Finalist vendors must follow the City's pre-defined script during their software demonstrations.
The proposal must be one electronic PDF copy, in the order defined in the response format table, not exceeding 100 total pages excluding sample contracts.
The response must include one completed copy of the Requirements document in MS Word format, with the Word format unmodified.
Proposals should be emailed to the City contact at Thuch.Mam@FederalWayWA.gov.
All data, materials and documentation originated and prepared for the City under this solicitation belong to the City.
Vendor questions about the RFP may be submitted by email to the City contact by August 28, 2024, 3:00 p.m. PT.
Vendor responses should include the sections outlined in the Proposal Response Format; deviation may lead to the response being deemed non-responsive and disqualified.
Marketing literature should not be included in the proposal.
The proposal must begin with a cover letter that is an executive summary of the proposed software and services, limited to two pages.
The vendor must complete the Pricing Summary from Exhibit A, indicating costs for software and implementation services.
Pricing must be comprehensive, including all taxes and available discounts.
Pricing must remain valid for 180 days from the response date.
The vendor must price the software for the user counts defined in the RFP.
The vendor must provide a separate pricing sheet for each deployment option offered (SaaS or on-premises).
Implementation pricing must include all costs required for go-live, including software deployment, data conversion, system configuration, report development, testing and training.
The vendor must price ongoing license and maintenance for Years 1-10.
Financials software must be priced for 130 named users and 85 concurrent users.
Human Capital Management software must be priced for 400 FTEs and 744 W2s.

The proposal must include an implementation overview covering methodology, sample project plan, City and vendor resources, process improvement, change management, data conversion, testing, training and report development.
The proposal must include an overview of support services offered, including hours, response times, support tiers, post go-live services, backup and disaster recovery.
The proposal must include a technology overview covering architecture and deployment options, data centers, hardware, mobile, remote access, integration tools and software updates.
The proposal must include a security overview covering the security model, standards, SSO/SAML administration, multi-factor authentication and breach response.
The vendor must provide references from three current and two prior customers for the proposed software, using the Exhibit B forms.
Preference is for references from Washington State public sector clients.
The vendor must disclose any contract terminations or legal actions with customers in the past five years, describing each situation with the contracting party's name and address.
The proposal must include sample contract documents such as a statement of work, license agreement, maintenance or support agreements and service level agreements.
The vendor must document any exceptions it has to the RFP content.
The vendor's Requirements responses will be incorporated into the signed contract.
The vendor must provide a rating and a comment for every item in the Requirements document; blank responses may cause rejection.
The vendor must not include hyperlinks in the Requirements document.
The vendor must not modify the format, font or numbering of the Requirements section or insert page breaks.
Requirement comments must give a substantive explanation; generic comments such as "Standard Functionality" are unacceptable.
Each line-item response in the Requirements document must be limited to 100 words.
The vendor must provide a certification of insurance before commencing any work.
An underwriter's endorsement with additional insured verbiage is required, and the surety must be admitted in the State of Washington.

The ERP solution must replace the City's Eden financial modules: General Ledger, Purchasing, Contract Management, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Project and Grant Accounting, and Capital Assets.
The ERP solution must replace the City's Eden Human Resources, Time and Attendance, and Payroll modules, as part of the ERP suite or integrated with it.
The ERP solution must replace the Quadrant cashiering system, as part of the ERP suite or integrated with it.
The ERP solution must replace the Excel-based budget process, as part of the ERP suite or integrated with it.
The ERP solution must replace the Excel-based preparation of the Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR), as part of the ERP suite or integrated with it.

The ERP solution must integrate with the retained systems NeoGov (recruiting), Power Time (police scheduling, time and attendance), Amanda and MBC.com (permitting, planning, land management), RecTrac (parks and recreation) and Class (Dumas Bay Conference Center).
Integration of the ERP solution with OpenGov (constituent transparency) and SharePoint (document management) is under review.
Enterprise asset management and fleet management, currently Excel shadow systems, are under review for inclusion in scope; their integration is to be determined.

component_records.title: Programme governance, compliance and contract management
component_records.description: A single governance workstream owns the commercial and legal spine of the engagement: a signed acknowledgement of the RFP's terms and conditions and exhibits, a written exceptions schedule, addenda tracking, and a proposal-error notification log so the City is notified of any ambiguity or discrepancy before submission. It delivers the insurance certification and underwriter's endorsement naming additional insureds with a Washington-admitted surety before any work starts, and it records the City's ownership of all data, materials and documentation produced under the contract. It also manages the City's prohibition on designating the whole submittal proprietary, the advance notice and justification of any confidential material, and the rule that proposals referencing non-City terms may be rejected. Monthly steering reporting, risk and issue logs, and change control run from contract signature through go-live and the support transition.

component_records.title: Integrated ERP and HCM module scope
component_records.description: The core of the offer is one integrated suite delivered as a single product set: the eight required financial modules (General Ledger, Budget, Project and Grant Accounting, Purchasing and Contract Management, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Capital Assets, Enterprise Cashiering) and the three required Human Capital Management modules (Human Resources, Time and Attendance, Payroll), all sharing one database, one security model and one reporting layer. Each module is configured to the functionality itemized in the Requirements document issued with the RFP, and a module-to-requirement mapping is published in the proposal so the City can trace every line of the Requirements document to a delivered module. Where the City prefers a best-of-breed HCM, the same financial suite is offered with the third-party HCM integrated in place of the native modules. This component is what makes the offer an integrated ERP replacement rather than a set of point applications.

component_records.title: Requirements response and scripted demonstration
component_records.description: The team completes the City's ERP Requirements document in unmodified MS Word, rating every line item 4, 3, 2, 0 or F with a specific comment of no more than 100 words that explains how the function is supported rather than restating the rating. Items rated 3 name the third-party application, items rated 2 carry an estimated modification cost, and items rated F carry an anticipated release month and year; no hyperlinks, no cross-references to other line items, no format or page-break changes. The same content is rehearsed into the December 2024 on-site demonstration, run strictly to the City-issued Demo Script and covering both script adherence and depth against the City's functional and technical requirements, with a pre-demo briefing attended by the named demo lead and product specialists. A question log captures clarifications submitted by the August 28, 2024 deadline and the answers issued on September 5, 2024.

component_records.title: Solution architecture, integration and technology alignment
component_records.description: A documented architecture covering the ERP platform, database, hosting model and accessibility approach, aligned to the City's IT strategy and offered in both SaaS and on-premises deployment shapes so the City can compare them. The component sets out the integration tools and methodology used to connect the financial suite to Human Capital Management, to the City's other systems and to any best-of-breed HCM option the City prefers, with named integration patterns, middleware and error handling. It also covers the security model and standards, SSO/SAML and multi-factor authentication, breach handling and communication, update cadence, and the data centre, redundancy and backup design behind the hosted option. This is the component that carries the technical depth the Technology criterion scores.

component_records.title: Phased implementation methodology and project plan
component_records.description: A defined, proven implementation methodology with a sample project plan showing phases, tasks, dependencies and dates, sequenced so that all modules in scope are live by January 1, 2027 within the March 2025 to January 2027 window. The plan is phased by module group, starting with financials and core HR data, then payroll and time and attendance, with each phase carrying design, configuration, conversion, test and cutover gates. It states City resources by role, responsibility and average hours per month, and vendor resources on the same basis, so the City can see the staffing commitment behind the date. Process improvement is built into design workshops, with the vendor's best practices proposed and the City approving each adoption, and a business change management methodology with named tools runs alongside. The plan is re-baselined at the January 2025 due diligence review and locked at contract negotiation.

component_records.title: Data conversion, report development and integration build
component_records.description: A per-module data conversion methodology that recommends, for each module, the years of history and the specific data elements to migrate from the City's legacy environment, with extract, cleanse, map, trial-load and reconciliation cycles and signed-off conversion results before each cutover. Report development covers the inventory of existing reports, the standard and custom report set to be delivered, the development and validation approach, and the handover of report-writing capability to City staff. Integration build delivers the interfaces identified in the architecture component, tested end to end against the City's systems. All of this work is priced inside the implementation services line so the City sees a go-live-complete number.

component_records.title: Testing, training and go-live readiness
component_records.description: A testing methodology and toolset covering unit, integration, regression, security, performance and user acceptance testing, with City-defined acceptance criteria and defect severity rules that gate each phase cutover. Training is delivered by role for the 130 named and 85 concurrent financial users and the 400 FTEs and 744 W-2s in Human Capital Management, using a train-the-trainer model, role-based materials, a sandbox environment and refresher sessions at go-live. Go-live readiness is a formal checklist per module: converted data signed off, interfaces proven, reports validated, users trained and support desk briefed. Cutover and hypercare plans cover the first weeks after each module goes live, with on-site vendor presence through the January 2027 final go-live.

component_records.title: Support, hosting operations and post-go-live services
component_records.description: A support model with stated support hours, guaranteed response times by severity, the resources assigned and the escalation path, presented as a baseline-versus-premium comparison so the City can choose its service level. It covers post-go-live tools and services, the backup strategy and its support arrangements, and disaster recovery covering backup, redundancy and location, again split between baseline and premium. User groups and conferences are described as part of the ongoing service, and the software update approach states whether updates are scheduled or automatic and on what timeline. Support is priced for Years 1 through 10 so the City sees the full ten-year cost of ownership.

component_records.title: Exhibit A pricing, deployment options and assumptions
component_records.description: The Exhibit A Pricing Summary is completed without altering its format, with a separate sheet for each deployment option (SaaS and on-premises) as the template requires. Year 1 software costs are itemized module by module for the eight financial modules and the three HCM modules, and implementation services are itemized across Implementation, Data Conversion, Training, Report Development, Integration, Travel and Other. Subscription and maintenance are shown for each of Years 2 through 10, with sub-totals for Software, Implementation and Maintenance/Licence and an overall Total. Pricing is built on 130 named and 85 concurrent financial users and 400 FTEs and 744 W-2s, is comprehensive including all taxes and available discounts, and is held valid for 180 days from the response date. Assumptions sit alongside the numbers, and every item rated 2 in the Requirements document carries its estimated modification cost here.

component_records.title: Vendor credentials, references and organisational evidence
component_records.description: A credentials pack evidencing organisational strength, viability and vision, a track record with government entities, and comparable city implementations of the proposed modules at similar size and scope, with preference given to Washington State public sector clients. References are submitted on the Exhibit B forms with three current and two prior customers, each listing customer name, employee count, population, contact name and title, telephone and email, software scope, implementation duration, go-live date and reason for change. The pack also discloses any contract terminated for convenience, non-performance or other reason, or any legal action with a customer, in the past five years, naming the contracting party and address. This is the evidence base for the Vendor criterion and the experience sub-score of Implementation.
